The biggest thing I learned form living in that area was that the lakes and rivers were fed through an underground aquifer, the Ogalalla (sp?) Aquifer. As humans pull water out of the ground using wells, etc. or harness water form rains for storage and don't let it get back into the aquifer, this lowers the highest point of the aquifer, draining spring fed lakes (which were simply depressions of land that dipped below the aquifer's highest level, and therefore filled up), and making river beds sandy and rocky for 90% of the year (except after torrential storms.)
